correctness.rationale: If a is bounded H_a=l2, one-class relation; if unbounded choose sparse coordinates with large weights so H_a is proper. For any two unbounded weights select injective σ with b_σ(n)>=a_n and Lx_σ(n)=sqrt(a_n/b_σ(n))x_n: contractive injective linear reduction with exact equality of weighted sums. The coordinate map T_a is continuous l2(norm)→R^N(product) and reduces E_a→E2. For E2→E_a, map each source coordinate t to Gaussian ψ_t(s)=exp(-(s-t)²/2) in L²(R), expand in ONB and put weighted, exponentially damped coordinates n(j,m). The weighted difference equals 2√π sum_j(1−exp(−(v_j−w_j)²/4)), equivalent to l2 difference; geometric tails guarantee product→Hilbert norm continuity. Any continuous additive homomorphism R^N(product)→l2 is finite-coordinate, hence cannot reduce E2. F_sigma follows finite partial sums. All quantifiers and topologies matter; no finite simulation replaces proof.
residual_risks: The argument depends on the explicit stated hypotheses; no unproved extension is claimed.

Dougherty and Hjorth, Reducibility and nonreducibility between ℓp equivalence relations (DOI:10.1090/S0002-9947-99-02290-5): Classifies benchmark l_p relations, not the explicit diagonal normed-Hilbert family or continuous additive obstruction.
